medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Albert Einstein College of Medicine provides a confidential and safe environment for M.D. students, Ph.D. students, and dual M.D./Ph.D. students to discuss academic and personal issues that could affect their journey through medical or graduate school.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leaves of absence may be granted on an individual basis for appropriate reasons.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
The Office of Student Life under the direction of Student Affairs is responsible for planning student events from Orientation through Commencement as well as supporting student clubs and activities. The office works with the entire Einstein community, meets regularly with the student council, mentors student clubs and creates social activities to foster the Einstein community. 
For more information, please see: https://einsteinmed.edu/education/student-affairs/student-activities/
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Located in the northeast Bronx, surrounded by private homes and apartment buildings and near the Westchester County border, the area combines small-town living with easy access to Manhattan. Close by are the Bronx Zoo, Botanical Gardens, Yankee Stadium, City Island (a fishing and sailing community), Orchard Beach, and the sprawling Pelham Bay Park, where there is hiking, swimming, horseback riding, golfing, and bicycling. Public transportation is plentiful and an Express bus to Manhattan stops in front of the Housing Entrance.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Housing is among the best in the country. Apartments are large, rents are low (utilities are included) and security is excellent . There are studios as well as one-and two-bedroom apartments which students share with a/c, fully equipped eat-in-kitchens, and ample closet space. Parking, laundry facilities, courtyard with lawn, outdoor tables and Adirondack chairs, community garden, BBQ grills, outdoor running track and tennis court, children's playground, and a large athletic facility are on the premises. Housing is available to all Einstein students and to their spouses or committed partners.  For gallery of housing photos see:  https://www.einsteinmed.edu/administration/auxiliary-services/housing/
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Einstein PRIDE seeks to create a healthy, welcoming, inclusive community among LGBTQIA students, faculty, staff and allies. PRIDE organizes social events on campus and engages in community events  that are open to all members of the Einstein community.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Einstein is committed to providing access and equal opportunities to all students, including those with disabilities. Einstein provides reasonable accommodation for known disabilities so that students have an equal chance to participate in academic and extracurricular programs. We provide guidance to faculty and staff to assure that students with disabilities are included without compromising standards, and to assure reasonable accommodation and program accessibility as required by law. (Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and the ADA of1990.) Students with documented learning disorders and students who require time-limited assistance in cases of illness or injury, may also apply for accommodations. The office of academic support and counseling at Albert Einstein College of Medicine provides students who are matriculated in our M.D. program, Ph.D. program, or the dual M.D./Ph.D. program with a variety of support services to ease the transition to medical and graduate school.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Physicians and Scientists do their best work when they are healthy and balanced. WellMed's goal at Einstein is to provide opportunities for students to adopt habits and attitudes that will contribute to their balance and well-being. By focusing on wellness during the formative years of medical and graduate school, students can become better healers, scientists, and role models for their patients and teams. See:  https://einsteinmed.edu/education/life-einstein/for-students/wellmed-health-wellness. In addition, the office of community engagement and outreach (OCEO) supports the development of excellent clinicians and scientists to become leaders in medicine and science.  For over four decades at Einstein, the OCEO and its predecessors have helped provide counseling and advising, academic monitoring, support services, resources and recruitment of students from various backgrounds. We broaden community awareness through the twenty-two biomedical pathway programs in our consortium.  Our retention program complements the support of other academic offices to promote personal and professional growth for all students.  The OCEO is supported by the larger institutional infrastructure and Einstein’s 2030 Strategic Plan in its work with medical students, graduate students in the biomedical sciences, faculty, and staff.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Albert Einstein College of Medicine is an academic community of more than 3,000 students, postdoctoral fellows, and faculty from across the nation and the world, living and learning in a great, global city where people enjoy the freedom to pursue their dreams. Our campus is in the northeast Bronx, where students enjoy the convenience and comfort of a quiet residential area with easy access to the culture and excitement of New York City. Our goal is for students to feel at home as part of the Einstein community. To this end, students, faculty, and administrative staff work together to create a student-centered experience. We understand that time in medical school isn’t just defined by time in class, on the wards, or in the lab. We offer many opportunities to enrich your experience both inside and outside of education and training settings, as well as options to tailor your education in ways that support your unique career goals.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Einstein operates a shuttle for Einstein ID card holders that travels between our campus, Montefiore Medical Center, and the local (180 Street) subway station.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The medical school leadership all have office hours. Einstein has a peer-tutoring system that is free and covers all aspects of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Longitudinal 4 year Becoming a Physician Course begins within weeks of matriculation
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: 17-month pre-clerkship curriculum, incorporating a doctoring course, is followed by clinical instruction and professional development activities.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Required clerkships: Internal Medicine and Primay Care, Surgery, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, Neurology, Obstetrics & Gynecology
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: There is an optional 2-week prematriculation biochemistry course. All students attend a 5-day Orientation the week prior to the first week of courses.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Einstein’s educational mission is to train students to understand and embrace their future roles as physicians. Caring for patients requires recognition of each patient’s individuality, and comfort with the uncertainty inherent in that experience. With the well-being of the patient as the focus of all our educational efforts, students learn to participate in the scientific endeavor of medicine, develop into critical thinkers and further our understanding of health promotion and disease management. We expect all Einstein graduates to demonstrate competency in the following seven areas: healer, scientist, advocate, educator, colleague, role model and lifelong learner.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: In addition to our curriculum being rich in foundation science and health equity, Einstein’s curriculum (1) enables its students to acquire the broad knowledge and skills needed to practice generalist medicine and (2) provides experiences that demonstrate to all students the attractions and rewards of careers in generalist disciplines. Health systems science instruction is robustly presented across the curriculum to enable engagement of learners in community and clinical settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
There are myriad opportunities for students attending Einstein. Research involvement can happen over months to years, in the summer between first and second year, in the fourth-year elective program and, for many of our students, during a year of dedicated research between the third and fourth year.  
Students can also perform research and receive MPH or MS degrees through the Einstein-CUNY MPH, Clinical Research Training Program and Bioethics Program.
See:  https://einsteinmed.edu/research

The Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP) was one of the three original MD/PhD programs started in 1964, and, with continuous NIH funding, maintains its successful tradition of training physician scientists.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText:
Preclerkship phase: Interdisciplinary biomedical & health system sciences and systems-based courses, longtudinal Becoming a Physician Course
Clinical phase: clerkships, acting internships, electives
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service is an integral component of the Einstein experience and includes a longitudinal Service Learning Course across the four year curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Montefiore Medical Center; Jacobi Medical Center, and other hospitals and community centers in the Bronx, Queens, Westchester County and the Hudson Valley
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: Preclinical courses are pass/fail whereas clinical rotations are honors/high pass/pass/low pass/fail. Written narratives accompany courses with significant faculty contact, including clerkships.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Einstein provides clinical education across multiple clinical sites in the Montefiore Health System as well as with a network of affiliates in New York City, Westchester County and the Hudson Valley including a longstanding relationship with Jacobi Medical Center in the Bronx. The curriculum combines a solid foundation in the biomedical and health systems sciences and rigorous, hands-on clinical training with the flexibility to pursue research interests and to meet the healthcare needs of the Bronx, the greater New York metropolitan area, and beyond. Specific educational program objectives guide students to meet competencies to become physicians who are competent as healers, scientists, advocates, educators, colleagues, role models, and lifelong learners. There are 2000+ full-time faculty members; 1000+ MD, MD/PhD and PhD students; 10,000+ alumni.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Albert Einstein College of Medicine is a research-intensive medical school. For more than 60 years, our faculty and staff have set the standard for excellence in medical and graduate education and patient-centered clinical care, and have made major contributions to scientific research enhancing human health in our communities and beyond. Our mission is to prepare students to become knowledgeable, compassionate physicians and innovative scientific investigators, and to create new knowledge. At Albert Einstein College of Medicine, we train M.D. students to understand and embrace their future role as physicians. We foster an environment in which students learn from each other, our expert clinical and research faculty, and our community, through clinical experiences and service-learning opportunities. Our students develop into critical thinkers who embrace the science of medicine and further our understanding of health.

We educate future leaders who want to change medicine. Not just within a discipline, but in how healthcare is practiced. Compassion, collaboration, and collegiality are the hallmarks of an Einstein education. From our mission aligned admission process and noncompetitive pass/fail system to our service learning course and opportunities for research and dual degrees, we value and support each student as you pursue your interests and launch your career in medicine. As an Einstein graduate, you leave school prepared to excel as a healer, scientist, advocate, educator, colleague, role model, and life-long learner.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Please see:  https://einsteinmed.edu/education/md-program/md-admissions/admissions-requirements .  Updates should always be sent to the AMCAS Letter Writer Service. Applicants who are invited for interview will be provided a link to which their updates can be sent.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Applicants who have completed their pre-medical coursework as an undergraduate or post-baccalaureate student at a college or university where there is a Pre-Professional Advisory Committee are required to submit a letter of recommendation from that Committee or provide an explanation why not. Applicants who do not have a Pre-Professional Advisory Committee must have at least two letters of recommendation from faculty members who have taught the applicant in the classroom setting. It is required that one of these letters be from a faculty member in the department of the applicant’s major, and the other from a science faculty member (2 science letters from 2 different faculty members in the same department are acceptable). Applicants whose post-baccalaureate, pre-professional advisor does not provide a statement regarding good standing, must request a letter from the Dean of Students or Registrar at their undergraduate college affirming good standing status.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Applicants invited for an interview will meet, virtually, with one member of the Admissions Committee. The interview usually lasts 30-60 minutes, and is conducted by a clinician or scientist from the committee.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Einstein is aware of the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and will accept pre-requisite science courses taken on-line and/or with a pass/fail grade, for the spring 2020, fall 2021 and spring 2021 semesters.  Applications will not be considered until MCAT scores are available. Letters of recommendation and the Supplemental Application must be received by December 1. 

International students are not eligible to apply.

Einstein strives to matriculate outstanding students whose academic accomplishments, clinical experiences, community service and research indicate that they will become exceptional healers, educators, colleagues, patient advocates, scientists, role models and life-long learners. We are committed to identifying individuals who already have demonstrated the qualities of compassion, empathy, kindness, creativity, professionalism, leadership and maturity. A diverse student body is consistent with the history and mission of Einstein and supports a key educational objective to raise the cultural awareness and competence of our graduates.  

Medicine is increasingly appreciated as a discipline that requires skills and abilities that are acquired through experiences and venues both inside and outside the classroom. 

In response and to prepare applicants for mission-aligned review that will evaluate, equally, personal characteristics and academic readiness for medical school, Einstein has instituted a competency-based admissions process.  We believe that this approach will allow applicants the opportunity to demonstrate the complex personal dimensions that contribute to being a good doctor, in addition to the cognitive capabilities that have traditionally identified applicants as being ready for the academic rigor of medical school.  This "competency-based" approach also provides candidates greater flexibility, for example, by substituting laboratory experience gained, while employed, for laboratory and or course requirements taken in school, or by substituting online courses that free up time to pursue interests that enhance the applicant's level of maturity and readiness for the medical profession. 

The Committee on Admissions will use the entire application to ensure that the candidate has demonstrated reasonable accomplishment of all of the identified competencies; this includes the AMCAS application, academic record, personal comments, roster of experiences, letters of recommendation, the Einstein secondary application, written and verbal communication with the Admissions Office, and interview (where applicable).

There are 4 competencies (which can be viewed in detail at:  https://www.einsteinmed.edu/education/md-program/admissions/application-procedure/
1.Co-Curricular Activities and Relevant Experiences 
2.Communication Skills 
3.Personal and Professional Development 
4.Knowledge 

Whereas course work at a four-year college or university is our benchmark, if a student meets a competency component via an alternate route such as through laboratory experience, through an advanced placement course, a course taken at a community college, a course taken abroad (during a semester abroad for which the undergraduate U.S. degree-granting institution gives credit, or for which AMCAS will verify and report the grade), or an online course, he or she should seek guidance from his or her advisor to ensure that the option meets the above guidelines as well as the rigorous academic standard required by the Albert Einstein College of Medicine.

MCATS
Applicants must take the MCATs not later than September of the year preceding matriculation and not later than three years prior to application.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: 3.0 is a suggested GPA but the whole application will be reviewed, especially for challenges that were overcome.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Applicants are encouraged to complete their science pre-requisites at a 4-year college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Interviewed applicants, only,  may submit their letters of intent, interest and notice of significant updates or achievements via a link to the Applicant Portal that will be sent to interviewed students on the Friday following their interview, and will be included in an email that invites the applicant to complete an Interview Day Survey.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The Technical Standards for medical students define the essential abilities and attributes required to complete Albert Einstein College of Medicine’s (“Einstein’s”) MD program and to deliver safe, effective, and compassionate patient care.  These standards help ensure that, with or without reasonable accommodation, all students are able to meet the academic, clinical, and professional demands of medical education.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Every attempt is made to assist students in meeting their financial obligations to the college and their essential personal needs. About 50% of students receive institutional loans and/or scholarships; about 80% qualify for outside loans and/or grants.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Einstein and Yeshiva University are committed to making studies affordable.  In addition, financial  support is provided to encourage students to pursue their interests. For example, students who have a customized schedule or who have extended their four-year stay to study abroad or pursue research, pay only four years tuition. Tuition is payable at the start of the first and second halves of the school year, in two equal installments. Incoming first-year students must either pay their tuition or file the appropriate Stafford loan application two weeks prior to Orientation, or forfeit their place in the class at that time.  If accepted, international students who are not Canadian citizens must deposit with the Albert Einstein College of Medicine, not later than mid-July, funds to cover estimated tuition for the first two years of medical school, or forfeit their place in the class. Canadian citizens must deposit one-half of the first year's tuition in mid-July.  Details of the withdraw

medSchoolPrograms.info: 1. The Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and eight other participating New York State schools, of which Einstein is one, refer students to AMSNY/Jacobs School Post-Baccalaureate Program to complete a one-year program to strengthen their basic science skills.  Students who are accepted to AMSNY receive a provisional acceptance from the referring medical school, and upon the successful completion of the program, they matriculate at that school without having to reapply. Applicants must first apply via AMCAS to Einstein. 2.  (SURP) Each summer the Einstein Summer Undergraduate Research Program (SURP) brings together 50 college students for a one-of-a-kind opportunity to conduct laboratory research at Einstein, which is one of the world's top-ranking scientific institutions. The program is designed for undergraduates with a strong background in science who are considering a research career.

medSchoolPrograms.programLength: The Einstein-CUNY MD-MPH program is designed to be completed in five years, with the bulk of the MPH courses fitting into a gap year within the MD program.

medSchoolPrograms.info: 1. The Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP) at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine (Einstein) is one of the nation’s oldest. Continuously funded by the NIH since 1964, the Einstein MSTP has 500 illustrious Alumni  with careers spanning the spectrum from basic science research to clinical medicine and many variations in between. 2. The Master of Science (M.S.) in Clinical Research Methods is attained through the Clinical Research Training Program (CRTP). This intensive  2-year program is designed for those pursuing a career in investigator-initiated, hypothesis-driven clinical research. 3. The Master of Science in Bioethics can be earned on a flexible timeline. It can be attained by attending full time for 12 months, or part time spreading courses over 2.5 years; or an alternate flexible timing path can be created to meet specific needs.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Beginning February 20, you may select the “Plan to Enroll” feature if you think you may attend Einstein.

First round of acceptance, wait list and rejection after interview notice. Offers of acceptance must be acknowledged by completion of the online Acceptance Acknowledgement Form, the Criminal Background Check (CBC) and the online Technical Standards Acknowledgement Form within two weeks of the date of the letter of acceptance if before April 30; 5 business days if after April 30.
Deposit to hold place in the class
Beginning April 30, applicants must select the school of choice and hold only 1 accept and withdraw from all other places at which they are holding a place.

From April 15 - April 30, narrow your selection(s) to no more than three schools, and withdraw your acceptance(s) from all other schools; Until April 30, applicants can, continue to hold other acceptances, remain on alternate lists, and continue to interview at other schools. If applicants receive new offers, they can update this selection, but select only one school at a time.
Official transcripts for all accepted students are required from all schools attended, whether or not a degree was conferred.
Commit to Enroll for the MD is July 18 (May 16 for the MSTP)

We believe that this approach will allow applicants the opportunity to demonstrate the complex personal dimensions that contribute to being a good doctor. In addition to the cognitive capabilities that have traditionally identified applicants as being ready for the academic rigor of medical school, this competency-based approach also provides candidates greater flexibility, for example, by substituting laboratory experience gained, while employed, for laboratory and or course requirements taken in school, or by substituting online courses that free up time to pursue interests that enhance the applicant's level of maturity and readiness for the medical profession.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText:
Applicants must be able to demonstrate an understanding of the clinical aspects of the career on which they are about to embark. As such, they must engage in meaningful experiences, at home or abroad, that provide exposure to clinical settings involving patient care and also provide opportunities for interaction with and learning from persons who are living with illness and/or disabilities.  

Recognizing  that time is limited, however, and that work, research and other activities can contribute to a student's overall preparedness for medical school but might compete with time that would have been devoted to clinical exposure, Einstein will consider, holistically, the full set of activities described in a candidate's application.
